newsitem.title: USA: U.S. may evacuate more Kurds from Iraq.
newsitem.headline: U.S. may evacuate more Kurds from Iraq.

text.p: The United States said on Wednesday it was considering evacuating thousands more Kurds from northern Iraq because it believed they were at risk.
State Department deputy spokesman Glyn Davies said the Kurds being considered for airlift worked for private voluntary organisations that helped maintain the U.S.-led safe haven in northern Iraq.

The programme of assisting and protecting Kurds in the region collapsed after troops of Iraqi President Saddam Hussein several weeks ago entered the north to help one Kurdish faction defeat its rival in armed conflict.
"No decision has been made on this (but) it is our inclination to do this if we can," Davies said.
The United States recently evacuated to the Pacific island of Guam via Turkey 2,100 Kurds and their families who were working directly for U.S. government in northern Iraq.
Davies said the new evacuation under discussion would involve "thousands" more Kurds. "We do believe there are credible threats to this second group of people," he said, refusing to go into details.
Davies also said he could not discuss logistics for the evacuation because those plans are still under discussion.

He said the United States did not evacuate these Kurds with the first wave last week because its "first loyalty" was to its direct employees who were considered at greatest risk of attack by Saddam's forces. Also, the U.S. employees were all in one place and clearly identified, he said.
